items.title: Alap / Pro / Add-on Capability Matrix
scope: Alap is a complete professional webshop and competitive baseline for ordinary day-to-day commerce; it is not an artificially crippled store

Alap does not expose authorable Special Commerce shopping engines: its storefront may be visually just as strong as Pro, but merchant/customer experiences such as Guided Finder, Composer, Configurator, Compatibility, Compare/Spec, Profile/Context, Release/Drop, Interactive Scene and Recipe Commerce are Pro capabilities
Pro is the business-system and enhanced-shopping layer: Digital Office, advanced B2B governance, advanced automation/analytics/intelligence, operational optimization and Special Commerce engines

both Alap and Pro use the same 42 design families, the same full manual Builder, the same canonical commerce authorities and the same storefront runtime; package differences are server-authoritative entitlements, never lower-quality designs or separate template forks

Digital Office is wholly Pro-only: no Team Chat, shared mailbox/inbox, communication workspace, tasks, approvals, staff profiles, leave/delegation, sending center, shared communication history/templates or Digital Office workforce surface may leak into Alap

Alap still includes ordinary transactional webshop email, Form Wizard delivery to an external merchant email address, newsletter/basic campaign sending and customer-facing notifications; these do not create a Digital Office workspace

baseline multi-location/multi-warehouse inventory is Alap; automated cross-location routing, split-fulfillment optimization, depot/address-aware source selection and Smart Stock/procurement optimization are Pro
simple ready-made automation recipes and single event-to-action rules are Alap; multi-condition, branching and multi-step governed workflows are Pro

ordinary company billing and simple customer groups/segments are Alap; company-account B2B purchasing governance, RFQ/offer, contract pricing, approval/spending/credit policy and maker-checker are Pro

provider integrations required to operate a normal Hungarian webshop are Alap; merchant-facing advanced API/webhook/integration-management depth is Pro, while connector-specific external/variable costs may remain Add-on
AI Builder, subscriptions, advanced AR/3D and similarly specialized or variable-cost capabilities remain Add-on/post-launch rather than being forced into Pro

shared internal engines may technically power ordinary storefront primitives, but an Alap merchant cannot configure, instantiate or publish Pro Special Commerce experiences through Builder/template entitlements
package boundaries may be refined from real usage later, but a later recommendation cannot silently override an explicit PO entitlement decision

benchmarkBasis.policy: Alap remains a complete competitive professional webshop for ordinary commerce; Pro differentiates through larger-operation tooling and enhanced shopping/commerce engines while design quality remains equal.
reconciliationNotes: The detailed competitor benchmark is a floor for normal webshop capability, not a reason to expose Shoperation's differentiated Special Commerce engines in Alap.
A later accepted entitlement decision records Guided Finder, Composer, Configurator, Compatibility/Fitment, Compare & Spec and Profile Context as Pro capabilities.

The current PO decision makes the package rule explicit: equal design quality does not imply equal shopping-engine capability; Pro templates gain the Special Commerce engines behind the shared design/runtime.
Later explicit PO decisions supersede older assistant suggestions or earlier temporary entitlement placements where they conflict.

customer purchase-order/reference number is a first-class RFQ/offer/order attribute; merchant policy may make it mandatory for B2B purchasing and it is carried as an immutable order/invoice handoff snapshot

quote conversion probability remains hidden until at least 3 months of tenant-specific learning and at least 30 closed quote outcomes; elapsed time alone never activates the KPI and insufficient confidence hides it again

domain modules such as inventory, CRM/B2B, customer service, Digital Office and operational recovery must reuse this workflow authority instead of creating separate automation engines
the workflow engine does not itself invent business decisions or gain direct unrestricted commerce mutation authority

supervised operation must collect structured outcome evidence about recommendations/proposals: whether merchants viewed, accepted, rejected, modified or ignored them and what observable outcome followed where attribution is valid
self-evaluation means measuring recommendation usefulness, accuracy, confidence calibration, false positives/negatives and merchant adoption; it does not grant the system self-approval authority
resource investment in broader autonomy is evidence-gated rather than assumed from technical possibility

items.title: Controlled Integration Framework
scope: closed/walled-garden integration model: external systems receive only the smallest explicit capability required for the connector's job
Market Ready foundation includes tenant-scoped, revocable/expiring credentials, allowlisted scopes, webhook/event delivery, retry/dead-letter evidence, audit and provider/connector lifecycle controls
least privilege is mandatory: a printer-like connector that needs one function receives that function, not broad filesystem, tenant-data, admin or generic runtime access
no arbitrary third-party code execution, plugin-installed runtime, generic SQL/RPC/database proxy or broad permission bundle
provider adapters and approved ERP/WMS/accounting/operational connectors reuse this foundation
a public/open App Store ecosystem is not a Market Ready blocker; any later marketplace remains curated, reviewed and permission-scoped rather than Shopify-style unrestricted extension execution
external third-party software integrates out-of-process through governed APIs/webhooks/connectors; it does not install arbitrary runtime code inside Shoperation
compatibility is contract-based rather than vendor-based: any external system capable of the supported secure protocols may integrate through an approved connector or a bounded translation bridge
legacy/proprietary systems without suitable native APIs may require a separately reviewed external bridge/agent; this does not expand Shoperation runtime permissions

items.title: Developer Integration Sandbox + Certification Kit
scope: provide a non-production developer environment for approved external connector/application developers without granting access to real merchant data or Shoperation internal runtime
sandbox tenant/test data plus stable documented API contracts, app/connector registration, least-privilege scope selection and revocable test credentials

webhook simulator/replay tooling, idempotency examples, signed-event verification examples, rate-limit/error simulations and reference integration examples/SDKs where they materially reduce integration mistakes
machine-checkable connector capability manifest declares exactly which resources, actions, events and permissions the integration requires

contract/conformance test suite and certification harness verify scope use, tenant isolation, retries, webhook handling, security boundaries, version compatibility and failure behavior before production approval
API versioning, compatibility and deprecation policy prevents silent connector breakage
production access is a separate reviewed activation step with narrower-or-equal scopes to the certified sandbox declaration
no arbitrary code installation, no generic filesystem/database access and no blanket tenant permission request model

items.title: Sandbox / Test Mode + Integration Self-test

payment self-test

cost per tenant/order, database, egress, storage, search and queue observability
load/scale decisions tied to measured evidence

backup/restore and disaster-recovery readiness with observable recovery evidence

items.title: Shoperation Core Capability Complete
scope: Stage 1 maturity gate: the actual webshop operating system is functionally complete for the accepted Hungarian Market Ready scope before Builder completion work resumes
historical operational or hardening labels on lower-level components do not satisfy this gate by themselves

the gate covers tenant/RBAC/workforce, admin/onboarding, catalog/product/media/CSV/bulk/barcode, inventory/multi-location, order/payment/shipping/invoice/returns/refunds, promotions/SEO/customer account, B2B, Digital Office/communications, migration, controlled integrations, sandbox, scale/cost, privacy/security/backup/observability, shared storefront runtime and launch-classified Special Commerce
no higher-layer Builder, Factory or template proof can compensate for a missing Core capability

items.title: Shoperation Core Operational / Adversarial Audit
scope: mandatory Core closure stage after webshop-system capability implementation and before Unified Shoperation Product Experience, Builder or template production can proceed

audit the actual end-to-end webshop operating system, not Builder/template visuals: identity/RBAC/tenant isolation, onboarding/admin flows, catalog/variants/media/CSV/bulk/barcode, inventory/multi-location, order/payment/shipping/invoice/returns/refunds, promotions/SEO/customer account, B2B, Digital Office/communications, migration, integrations, tax, sandbox, scale/cost, privacy/security/backup/observability and launch-classified Special Commerce

normal functional proof is insufficient: execute adversarial and failure-path proof including malformed/stale data, duplicate callbacks, partial provider outage, timeouts/retries, concurrency/race conditions, reservation/transfer conflicts, cross-tenant access attempts, permission escalation attempts, partial imports/migrations, refund/order/payment mismatches and recovery/rollback scenarios
include realistic load, soak, scale, restore/disaster-recovery and operational observability exercises where applicable
Completion Truth rule: higher-layer Builder/template success cannot compensate for missing or partial Core evidence

audit output must explicitly identify high-value missing capabilities, design weaknesses, unsafe assumptions or commercially meaningful gaps; recommendations are surfaced to the Product Owner rather than silently omitted
any newly proposed capability discovered by the audit requires explicit PO acceptance before it becomes roadmap scope
Core may advance only when findings are fixed, deliberately accepted as bounded risk, or explicitly deferred by PO with documented rationale and evidence
